source.title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs

accepted.question_text: For a tournament, meaning an orientation of a complete graph, that contains at least one directed cycle, is there always an arc whose reversal decreases the total number of directed cycles?

evidence.quote: which claims that every oriented graph (i.e., a digraph without cycles of length 2), which has a cycle (in this paper all cycles and paths in digraphs are directed), contains an arc whose reversal decreases the number of cycles.
However, the conjecture restricted to tournaments, posed by Reid and Beineke [63] in 1978, remains open.
An orientation of a complete graph is called a tournament

accepted.question_text: For an Euler oriented graph, meaning a connected oriented graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, that contains at least one directed cycle, is there always an arc whose reversal decreases the total number of directed cycles?
accepted.context_brief: Adam conjecture for Euler oriented graphs

evidence.quote: which claims that every oriented graph (i.e., a digraph without cycles of length 2), which has a cycle (in this paper all cycles and paths in digraphs are directed), contains an arc whose reversal decreases the number of cycles.
It seems to us that another interesting case is that of Euler oriented graphs, i.e., oriented graphs in which the in-degree of every vertex equals its out-degree;
A directed multigraph is Euler if it is connected and for every vertex x ∈ V (D), d +(x) = d−(x).

accepted.question_text: Let D be a finite digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k. Must D contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 Every digraph of minimum out-degree k and order n has a cycle of length at most ⌈ n k ⌉.

accepted.question_text: Let D be a finite digraph with minimum out-degree k. Must D contain k directed cycles C1, C2, ..., Ck that can be ordered so that, for every j at most k, the union of the earlier cycles C1, ..., Cj-1 and the cycle Cj have at most one vertex in common?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2 Every digraph D of minimum out-degree k contains a sequence C1, C2, . . . , Ck of cycles such that Sj−1 i=1 Ci and Cj have at most one vertex in common for all j ≤ k.
Conjecture 3.2 was proved for tournaments by Havet, Thomass´e and Yeo [48]. However, there is much less progress in our understanding of Conjecture 3.2 than of Conjecture 3.1.

accepted.question_text: Can the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture be verified for fixed small values of the minimum out-degree k, beginning with the currently first unsettled case k = 6?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 Verify Conjecture 3.1 for small values of k starting from k = 6.

accepted.question_text: Does the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture hold for multipartite tournaments, meaning orientations of complete multipartite graphs: does every such digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Does Conjecture 3.1 hold for multipartite tournaments?
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.

accepted.question_text: Does the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture hold for Euler digraphs, meaning connected directed multigraphs in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree: does every such digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 Does Conjecture 3.1 hold for Euler digraphs?
A directed multigraph is Euler if it is connected and for every vertex x ∈ V (D), d +(x) = d−(x).

accepted.question_text: Given a finite digraph D and a positive integer k, if the minimum out-degree of D is at least 2k - 1, must D contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3 Let D be a digraph and k ∈ Z>0. If δ +(D) ≥ 2k − 1 then D contains k vertex-disjoint cycles.

accepted.question_text: Can the Bermond-Thomassen vertex-disjoint-cycles conjecture be verified for multipartite tournaments: does every multipartite tournament with minimum out-degree at least 2k - 1 contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4 Verify Conjecture 3.3 for multipartite tournaments.
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite directed or undirected graph, and let lambda(G) be the number of vertices in a longest path of G. For every natural number q with 0 < q < lambda(G), must the vertices of G be partitionable into two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs A and B such that lambda(A) is at most q and lambda(B) is at most lambda(G) - q?

evidence.quote: A partition of G is a pair (A, B) of vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of G such that V (A)∪ V (B) = V (G). Let λ(D) denote the number of vertices in a longest path of D.
Conjecture 4.1 Let G be a directed or undirected graph. For every natural number q with 0 < q < λ(G) there is a partition (A, B) of G such that λ(A) ≤ q and λ(B) ≤ λ(G) − q.
For undirected graph, the conjecture was first formulated in 1981 (see [37]), and it is still open.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite directed graph, and let lambda(G) be the number of vertices in a longest directed path of G. For every natural number q with 0 < q < lambda(G), must the vertices of G be partitionable into two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs A and B such that lambda(A) equals q and lambda(B) equals lambda(G) - q?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 Let G be a directed graph. For every natural number q with 0 < q < λ(G) there is a partition (A, B) of G such that λ(A) = q and λ(B) = λ(G) − q.
It seems that this conjecture has not been studied in literature yet.

accepted.question_text: For acyclic digraphs with m arcs, let h(m) be the minimum, over all such digraphs, of the maximum size of a directed cut, where a directed cut (X, Y) consists of all arcs from X to Y. What is the infimum alpha_0 of alpha > 0 such that h(m) = m/4 + O(m^alpha) for all m >= 1?
accepted.context_brief: maximum directed cuts in acyclic digraphs

evidence.quote: For directed graphs, the directed cut (X, Y ) is the set of arcs from X to Y .
Corresponding to g(m), we can define a function h(m) for all acyclic digraphs with m arcs.
Problem 5.1 What is the infimum α0 of α > 0 such that, for m ≥ 1, h(m) = m 4 +O(mα)?

accepted.question_text: For acyclic directed multigraphs and weighted acyclic digraphs whose arc weights are at least 1, determine the exact asymptotic exponent for the error term above one quarter of the total arc count or total arc weight, closing the known gap between upper exponent 3/4 and lower exponent 3/5 for the corresponding functions h_mu and h_omega.
accepted.context_brief: weighted and multigraph directed cut exponent

evidence.quote: Very recently, Ai et al. [4] extended Alon’s results to acyclic directed multigraphs and weighted acyclic digraphs.
let Dω be the set of weighted digraphs in which every arc has weight at least 1
As we can see there is still a gap between 3 4 and 3 5 . Thus, it is natural to ask for the exact value.

accepted.question_text: Does every sink-free finite digraph D have a quasi-kernel Q with size at most |V(D)|/2? Here a quasi-kernel is an independent vertex set Q such that every vertex outside Q can reach some vertex of Q by a directed path of length one or two.

evidence.quote: An independent set X of a digraph D is a quasi-kernel if for every y 6∈ X, either there is x ∈ X such that y→x or there are x ∈ X and z 6∈ X such that y→z→x.
Conjecture 6.1 Every sink-free digraph D = (V (D), A(D)) has a quasi-kernel of size at most |V (D)| 2 .

accepted.question_text: For every n-vertex finite digraph D with sink set S, does D have a quasi-kernel Q satisfying |Q| <= (n + |S| - |N_D^-(S)|)/2, where N_D^-(S) is the set of vertices with arcs into S?

evidence.quote: In [53], Kostochka et al. gave an equivalent conjecture for all digraphs.
Conjecture 6.2 Let D be an n-vertex digraph, and let S be the set of sinks of D. Then D has a quasi-kernel Q such that |Q| ≤ n + |S| − |N − D (S)| 2 .

accepted.question_text: Is there a universal positive real constant c < 1 such that every sink-free digraph of order n has a quasi-kernel Q with |Q| <= c n?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 [34] Is there a positive real c < 1 such that for every sink-free digraph of order n, there exists a quasi-kernel Q with |Q| ≤ cn?

accepted.question_text: Other than the directed cycle of length 4, does there exist a connected sink-free digraph of order n for which every quasi-kernel has size n/2?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2 Besides a cycle of length 4, is there a connected sink-free digraph such that all its quasi-kernels are of size n 2 ?

accepted.question_text: Does every oriented graph D have a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood has cardinality at least its out-neighborhood, that is, |N++(v)| >= |N+(v)|?

evidence.quote: Seymour’s Second Neighborhood Conjecture (SSNC) (see e.g., [29]) is one of the most interesting open problems on digraphs.
Conjecture 7.1 Every oriented graph D has a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood N ++(v) is not smaller than its out-neighborhood N +(v).

accepted.question_text: Can Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture be verified for split oriented graphs and for multipartite tournaments? A split digraph has its vertices partitioned into a semicomplete part and an arc-less part, and a multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph.
accepted.context_brief: Seymour conjecture for split and multipartite classes

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 Verify that Seymour’s Conjecture holds for (a) split oriented graphs, (b) multipartite tournaments.
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.
A split digraph D is a digraph in which vertices can be partitioned into two sets X and Y such that D[X] is a semicomplete digraph and D[Y ] is an arc-less digraph.

accepted.question_text: What is the largest constant c such that every oriented graph has a vertex v satisfying |N++(v)| >= c |N+(v)|, where N++(v) is the second out-neighborhood and N+(v) is the out-neighborhood of v?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 Find the largest coefficient c such that for any oriented graph, there is a vertex v satisfying the inequality |N ++(v)| ≥ c|N +(v)|.

accepted.question_text: Does every oriented graph D have a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood has cardinality at least its in-neighborhood, that is, |N++(v)| >= |N-(v)|?

evidence.quote: Sullivan [64] posed the following variation of Seymour’s Conjecture.
Conjecture 7.2 Every oriented graph D has a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood N ++(v) is not smaller than its in-neighborhood N −(v).

accepted.question_text: Does every planar oriented graph admit a 2-coloring of its vertices such that each color class induces an acyclic subdigraph?

evidence.quote: An acyclic k-coloring of a digraph D is a mapping c : V (G) → [k] such that for every i ∈ [k], c −1 (i) induces an acyclic subgraph of D.
Conjecture 8.1 Every planar oriented graph has an acyclic k-coloring with k ≤ 2.

trace.notes: Normalized URL https://zbmath.org/8011082 as a zbMATH resolver record. Browser fetch of the zbMATH page/API did not expose readable full text; local workflow CSV mapped the id to DOI 10.11845/sxjz.2023007a and title Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs. Exact DOI/title search found the CCJ publisher page and direct PDF. Shell curl could not resolve external hosts in this sandbox, so extraction used the browser-readable PDF URL.

Rewrote Problem 6.2 as an extremal quasi-kernel example question.
